What is a Tsunami?

A tsunami is a series of extremely long waves caused by a large and sudden displacement of the ocean, usually the result of an earthquake below or near the ocean floor. (Tsunamis NOAA)

Tsunamis are caused when there is sudden water displacement on the ocean floor. This is regularly caused by earthquakes on convergent tectonic boundaries. However it can also be formed by landslides and volcanic activity. When these hazards occur it can be a sign that a tsunami will occur. (Tsunamis NOAA)

What disasters can Tsunamis cause?

Tsunamis can impact health, cause property damage, destroy resources, and cause economic debt. They mostly impact the shore but can reach past to separate countries. (Tsunamis NOAA)

Where do tsunamis typically occur and how often do they occur?

Tsunamis typically occur in the Pacific Ocean around the Ring of Fire, where there are many earthquakes and volcanoes. Japan, Russia and Indonesia are the most likely places to get a tsunami. (Tsunami locations NOAA)

Tsunamis occur typically twice in a year; however, tsunamis that cause damage on distant shores happen twice per decade. (US Tsunami)

Technology that helps us predict tsunamis

Humans have developed warning systems for when a tsunami comes, so citizens will know. We have also made forecasts to learn which earthquakes will cause tsunamis, so people will know if they need to evacuate.
